statutes.act: And Order Vi Rule 17 Of The Code

facts: By the impugned order dated 14th July, 1998 in C.R.P. No. 494/87, the learned Single Judge of the High Court of Kerala granted permission to the respondent to amend the application filed on 4.4.1978 under Section 20 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 for appointment of arbitrator to resolve the dispute between the parties.

On 30.3.1986, the respondent-Corporation filed an interim application being I.A. No.885 of 1986 for amending the pending application under Section 20 of the Act so as to convert the same as a plaint under Order VII Rule 1 cf the C.P.C for recovery of money.
The agreement contained an option clause which gave the respondent unilateral option to extend the contract by one year.
It is also admitted position that agreement contained a clause for arbitration in case of dispute;
On the basis of the communication, respondent-Corporation invited fresh tenders for the period commencing from 4th April, 1975.

As against this, respondent filed Petition (Original Suit No. 107/78) under section 20 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 on 4.4.1978, before the Subordinate Judge, Palghat praying that (i) the agreement be filed; (ii) an arbitrator be appointed and directed to proceed to adjudge the dispute in accordance with law and (iii) for a direction for costs and such further relief.

The respondent-Corporation also filed an application being Interlocutory Application No.1406 of 1978 under Section 34 of the Arbitration Act in Civil Suit No. 130 of 1978 for stay of further proceedings and for referring the dispute to the arbitrator.

Subsequently on 13th March, 1986, the respondent filed an application for amendment of the pending application under Section 20 of the Arbitration Act for converting it as a suit and praying for recovery of a sum of Rs. 1,74,067.08 from the appellant.
issues: Whether the High Court was justified in allowing the respondent's application to amend the pending application under Section 20 of the Arbitration Act?
Whether the trial court correctly rejected the respondent's application for stay of further proceedings and for referring the dispute to the arbitrator?
petitioner_arguments: The appellant argued that the agreement contained a clause for arbitration in case of dispute;
The appellant also argued that the amendment would introduce totally new cause of action and change the nature of suit.

The appellant further argued that the claim of the respondent to recover the alleged amount was barred by the period of limitation as it was pointed out that cause of action for recovery of the said amount arose in the year 1975 and the amendment application was filed on 30.3.1986.
respondent_arguments: The respondent argued that the learned Judge has not verified the provisions of Section 20 of the Arbitration Act.

The respondent also argued that the suit no. O.S. 107 of 1978 instituted by respondent contains all particulars that should contain in a regular suit, whether the suit is one under Section 20 or regular suit,
court_reasoning: Jurisprudentially speaking an arbitrator is only a delegate of judicial powers which essentially are the property of the State
In short it is not only the privilege of the Court but it is duty also 'to come to the assistance of the parties by the removal of the impasse and the extrication of their rights'.
holding: The appeal is allowed with costs.
The impugned order passed by the High Court of Kerala in C.R.P. No. 494/87 is quashed and set aside and the order passed by the trial court is restored.
